'''Peter Adalbert Wolff''' (November 15, 1923 – September 5, 2013) was an American physicist and [[Emeritus]] professor of the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], who worked in semiconductor research.<ref>{{citation|url=http://news.mit.edu/2013/peter-wolff-obituary|title=Semiconductor research pioneer Peter Wolff dies at 89|first=Sarah|last=Wright|date=October 2, 2013|newspaper=MIT News|publisher=Massachusetts Institute of Technology}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{citation|last=Lee|first=Patrick|date=December 2013|doi=10.1063/pt.5.6018|journal=Physics Today|title=Peter A. Wolff}}</ref> He is known for the [[Schrieffer–Wolff transformation]] used to solve the [[Kondo model]].

== Life ==
He earned his PhD in physics at [[UC Berkeley]] with [[Robert Serber]] as thesis advisor in 1951<ref>{{cite web|title=Robert Serber|website=Physics Tree|url=https://academictree.org/physics/peopleinfo.php?pid=28562}}</ref> and began his career at the [[Bell Telephone Laboratories]] the following year. 

Wolff and [[John Robert Schrieffer]] developed the [[Schrieffer–Wolff transformation]] in 1966 to solve the [[Kondo model]].<ref name=":0" />

Thereafter Wolff joined the physics department of [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (MIT) in 1970, becoming head of the [[condensed matter]] and [[atomic physics]] division.<ref name=":0" /> In the following years he hired [[Marc A. Kastner]], [[John Joannopoulos]] and [[Robert J. Birgeneau]].<ref name=":0" /> Together with P. M. Platzman, he coauthored the textbook ''Waves and Interactions in Solid State Plasmas'' in 1973.<ref name=":0" /> 

In 1976 he moved on to the directorship of the [[Research Laboratory of Electronics]] and then of the [[Francis Bitter Magnet Laboratory|Francis Bitter National Magnet Laboratory]] in 1981. Wolff left the director's chair in 1987 and retired from his faculty position in 1989 to become a fellow of the newly created [[NEC Research Institute]] at [[Princeton University]]. In 1994 he returned to MIT as the leader of the physics/industry forum for the physics department and remained a professor emeritus.<ref name=":0" />

Wolff died of [[Alzheimer's disease]] in 2013.<ref name=":0" />
